collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder and a child aged 6-12)

collection.description: A child challenges an elder who claims to have been the fastest runner: set the rules, or run it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has always claimed to have been the fastest runner in the village when (subject.he/she) was young. Today (friend) has challenged (subject.him/her) to a race: to the big palm and back. The other children have gathered to watch. (subject) is looking at the big palm, which is a good deal farther away than (subject.he/she) remembers.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Gladly," says (subject). "A walking race. No running. Fastest walker wins." (friend) agrees, a bit suspiciously. It turns out that (subject) is a tremendously fast walker, with a long, swinging stride, and wins by three steps. The children demand a running race next time. (subject) says (subject.he/she) will consider it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) runs. (subject.He/she) is not the fastest any more: (friend) is round the palm and back while (subject) is still on the way out. (subject) arrives a while later, puffing and laughing, and lifts (friend)'s arm into the air. "The fastest runner in the village," (subject.he/she) announces. "I'm only passing it on."
